incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended (ss. 13, 14, 15, 19, 66); Companies Regulations 2011 (reg. 12-14)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008; a (Pty) Ltd may be incorporated with zero authorized capital, and no escrow or paid-up capital account is required. Share consideration is determined in the MOI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, as registered by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, be and is hereby ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Company issue 100 ordinary no-par shares to the founding subscriber, credited as fully paid from the subscriber's contribution. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be fixed at the address filed with the Notice of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that the director be appointed as sole director and the secretary be appointed as company secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and comply with all tax registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a CIPC name search and submit Form CoR 9.1 to reserve the proposed company name for 20 business days; concurrently prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation governing share classes, director powers, and governance rules. If no name is required, proceed with a registration-number entity.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of incorporators' identity or passport documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, CIPC permits resubmission with alternative names on the same CoR 9.1 within the statutory window, or adoption of the registration number as the company name; an aggrieved applicant may also apply for reconsideration within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the signed MOI and annexure declarations via CIPC e-services, settle the prescribed registration fee electronically, and await issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of CIPC filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC will issue an electronic query identifying formal defects; the incorporator must correct and resubmit within 25 business days under Regulation 14(5), failing which the application is deemed refused and a fresh filing with new fees is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and SARS tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC and South African Revenue Service (SARS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation, then within 21 days of incorporation register the company at SARS for income tax, VAT (if the compulsory threshold is met), PAYE, UIF, and SDL, and appoint a public officer as the company's statutory tax representative.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of directors and public officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the registration, submit the outstanding documents through eFiling or at the local SARS branch; late-registration penalties may be remitted upon demonstrating reasonable cause and prompt remediation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership and statutory registers recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Beneficial Ownership Schedule (Form CoR 30.1) identifying all beneficial owners and their percentage interests, and maintain the securities register, directors' register, and MOI records; thereafter file the annual beneficial ownership confirmation with CIPC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects the schedule due to data mismatch or incomplete beneficial ownership detail, correct the filing with verified source documents and resubmit; non-compliance attracts penalties under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 2022.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and corporate governance adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the ratified first board resolution approving share allotment, registered office, and officer appointments, issue share certificates, open the corporate bank account with mandated signatories, and adopt governance policies including Conflict of Interest, Information Governance, and POPIA compliance.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective allotment or officer appointment may be validated by a subsequent board resolution or special resolution of shareholders, and corrected minutes or banking mandates may be re-executed if rejected by counterparties or regulators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the entity operates as a digital stock-photography marketplace with no physical manufacturing establishment; operational oversight lies solely with CIPC and SARS absent a classified industrial activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial, trade, or media licensing obligation attaches to ISIC 7420 digital service activity under South African law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), South Africa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is a digital service not listed under the NEMA Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations Listing Notices 1-3 (2014, as amended), and therefore requires no EIA report or registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by server-based stock-photography operations; any office function must comply with municipal wastewater and general waste bylaws under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

stage_2.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must hold a Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local Fire Prevention Bureau under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, maintain an electrical installation certificate of compliance (SANS 10142-1), and secure an occupational health clearance confirming registerable compliance with the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national unified revenue authority; corporate tax, VAT, customs, and exchange-control oversight are administered via the eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za; general domain www.sars.gov.za).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic Pty Ltd: incorporation under Companies Act 71 of 2008; automatic income-tax registration is triggered upon CIPC incorporation — SARS issues a 10-digit income tax reference number; VAT registration requires a separate VAT 101 application. A company must register as a VAT vendor if taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any 12-month period (mandatory) or electively from R50,000. Foreign entities without a SA permanent establishment must register for income tax only for SA-source income; foreign suppliers of electronic services must apply for VAT vendor status through the SARS 'Foreign Supplier of Electronic Services' registration procedure (VAT 101 plus incorporation certificate, foreign VAT/income-tax number, proof of bank account, and appointment of a local representative agent) where the R1,000,000 South-Africa-supplied electronic-services threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid entity election exists under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; a Pty Ltd is per se a resident company taxed on worldwide income at 27% (with 80% capital gain inclusion). Available statutory elections include: (i) Small Business Corporation progressive-rate election for qualifying companies with turnover below R20 million; (ii) headquarter-company status (s9I) election for foreign-focused groups; (iii) VAT group registration election (s50 VAT Act) for closely linked companies; (iv) CFC 'deemed high-tax' exclusion elections; and (v) pre-approval Binding Private Rulings (TAA s76) for hybrid instrument or export-service classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, as amended) — national single-stage destination-based consumption tax; no separate GST or sales/use tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: taxable supplies exceeding R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration from R50,000 of taxable supplies. Foreign suppliers of electronic services: mandatory registration when the value of electronic services supplied to South African recipients exceeds R1,000,000 in any 12-month period (regulations under the VAT Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or CTC-authorisation regime is currently in force. SARS operates a voluntary SARS eInvoicing solution using digitally signed XML/PDF e-invoices; statutory tax invoices must contain the s20 VAT Act particulars. The VAT 201 return is filed electronically (eFiling/API) monthly or bi-monthly. A mandatory phased e-invoicing mandate has been publicly signalled by SARS for large vendors (turnover above R10 million), but as at the current compliance date legacy electronic invoices remain valid and no per-invoice SARS clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Electronic services (including stock-photo licences and AI-generated visual asset downloads) supplied by a SA vendor to non-residents are zero-rated under the exported-services rule (s11(2)(l) VAT Act) where: (i) the recipient is a non-resident; (ii) the recipient is outside South Africa at the time of supply; (iii) the services are not directly connected with land or movable property situated in SA; and (iv) no SA permanent establishment of the recipient is involved. The supplier must retain documentary proof of non-resident status and foreign consumption of the supply (IP-address geolocation, billing address, payment-rail country, foreign tax identifiers). Supply to SA residents is standard-rated at 15%, subject to the supplier's input-VAT position; imported taxable services are reverse-charged on the SA recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) — required only for physical exports of goods; not applicable to pure digital stock-photo/electronic-service supplies
Bill of Lading — not applicable in the absence of physical movement of goods; digital supply evidenced by download/licence records
Inward Remittance Certificate — or equivalent foreign-currency settlement evidence (Stripe/PayPal payout reports, SWIFT/MT103) proving receipt of consideration from abroad
Zero-rated VAT invoice satisfying s20 VAT Act content and expressly stating the s11(2)(l) zero-rating basis
Licence/subscription agreement evidencing the non-resident customer and the scope of the digital asset licence
Non-resident evidence pack (IP geolocation, billing address, foreign tax number, passport or company extract)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating by comparing VAT returns, payment-rail settlement reports, and licence metadata. If documentary proof is absent or fraudulent, the zero rating is retrospectively clawed back and output VAT at 15% is assessed from the supply date, with interest (TAA s187 — prescribed quarterly rate, currently approximately 10.75% per annum) and understatement penalties under TAA ss222–223: 20% standard case, 25% for failure to take reasonable care, 50% for substantial understatement or no reasonable grounds, and 100% for intentional tax evasion or gross negligence; an additional 15%–25% applies to impermissible tax avoidance arrangements. Criminal prosecution under TAA s234/235 (fraudulent conduct) may carry fines and imprisonment of up to five years; VAT Act s60–s61 penalties further expose the vendor to penalties of up to double the tax involved. SARS may reopen completed assessments for up to five years (or indefinitely where fraud is established) under TAA s99–s100.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, with delegated powers to Authorised Dealers in foreign exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a centrally administered exchange-control regime. The ZAR is a restricted currency; convertibility is effectively open for current-account transactions with documentary support, while capital-account transactions require Authorised Dealer or FinSurv approval. Stock-photo licensing and AI visual-asset export revenue are current-account invisibles and can be converted to ZAR at the closing market rate without special permit, provided a balance-of-payments (BoP) declaration is made. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted annually where profits are demonstrably after-tax, supported by audited or independently reviewed financial statements, a completed dividend declaration form, SARS tax-clearance status, and 20% dividends withholding tax settlement (or a reduced treaty rate). Inward share-capital subscriptions are treated as foreign direct investment and are repatriable only after the inward BoP/FDI declaration is correctly filed and matched; outward capital transfers by residents beyond stated allowances require FinSurv approval. No material profit-remittance quota exists, but SARS compliance status and exchange-control declaration integrity are the controlling hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from digital services, licensing, and stock-photo/AI content sales must be received within 180 days from the date of invoicing or provision of the licensing right. Proceeds received in foreign currency through an Authorised Dealer must be converted into ZAR within 7 business days of receipt, unless the exporter holds a FinSurv-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with the same Authorised Dealer, in which case settlement may be deferred within the account but full repatriation remains mandated. The statutory regime does not impose a percentage surrender penalty to the central bank; rather, 100% of the export value is subject to repatriation and conversion obligations, and every export/service receipt must be declared to SARB via the Authorised Dealer BoP return. If the entity collects via PayPal, Stripe, or other payment aggregators, the aggregate proceeds must be routed into a licensed South African banking channel and the same 180-day surrender window applies from value date.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability Rating: Low-to-Medium as a primary bank and Medium as an ancillary collection channel. Legal constraints: a South African resident (Pty) Ltd must conduct foreign-exchange business through an Authorised Dealer; maintaining a foreign account with an offshore digital EMI (e.g., Mercury, Wise Business, Payoneer) constitutes an external asset requiring prior FinSurv approval or an approved general-allowance election, and must be reported annually. Offshore EMI settlement rails cannot legally be the final repository for export proceeds without a SARB/FinSurv foreign-account approval; funds must ultimately be repatriated into a permitted ZAR account. Accordingly, the entity should rely on domestic tier-one banks for primary clearing and treat any offshore EMI strictly as a pre-approved collection conduit subject to BoP declaration and full repatriation disclosure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended) does not impose a blanket statutory rule requiring all directors to appear physically; however, each bank's Risk Management Compliance Programme determines the CDD threshold. For a newly formed local (Pty) Ltd with South African directors and a standard stock-media business profile, remote onboarding via e-FICA and SmartFICA identity verification is increasingly accepted. For non-resident directors, foreign beneficial owners, or any PEP connection, a physical interview with the bank's compliance officer, or a notarised/attested face-to-face confirmation performed before a bank-approved overseas notary or embassy official, is effectively mandatory. The company must also file a beneficial-ownership declaration under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 28 of 2022 before the bank can complete onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered (Pty) Ltd less than 12 months old with no financial statements, no trading history, and a single shareholder subscribing nominal share capital from a non-FATF-equivalent jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC certificate and Memorandum of Incorporation; board resolution appointing authorised signatories and confirming the banking mandate; beneficial-ownership register and shareholders' register; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations supported by bank statements from the originating jurisdiction; detailed business plan covering the stock-photography/AI content platform, projected revenue, merchant-licence contracts with Stripe/PayPal; notarised passport copies and certified proof-of-address for all shareholders and directors; SARS income-tax clearance certificate for each 10%+ owner where applicable; sworn affidavit explaining the source of the initial share subscription and the absence of third-party or cash deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume cross-border inflows from micro-licensing settlements (USD/EUR) materially disproportionate to the small headcount and local operating cost profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly platform settlement statements from Stripe/PayPal with transaction-level reconciliation trails; executed licence and distribution agreements with the marketplace operator; royalty schedules and pricing tables evidencing per-image/AI-asset average transaction values; customer and country mix extracts; ISIC 7420 / NAICS 541922 scope certificate or business proof; management accounts linking recorded revenue to the platform net settlement; quarterly SARB BoP declarations confirming export proceeds reporting; appointment of a compliance officer under FICA and a documented transaction-monitoring policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or beneficial owner resident in a sanctions-watchlist or high-tax-risk jurisdiction, combined with a request for immediate activation of high-limit internet banking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence pack including corporate registry extract and registered-office verification from the foreign jurisdiction; certified passport copies and national-ID of all directors; foreign tax-residence certificates and SARS tax reference numbers; 12-month personal bank statements for all material shareholders; asset-and-liability and source-of-wealth schedule; sanctions and PEP screening clearances; governance documentation (board minutes) proving that local management exercises control over the ZAR account; senior manager interview or notarised attestation confirming beneficial ownership; staged transaction limits with gradual activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request to permit settlement of export proceeds through an offshore digital EMI or third-party aggregator without authorisation, or evidence of cryptocurrency/round-trip structures in the funding path.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written FinSurv/SARB approval or the annual general-allowance election under which the foreign account is held; completed annual external-asset returns to SARB; commercial justification for USD collection via the EMI; commitment letter agreeing to convert and repatriate all proceeds within the 180-day service-export window; FICA-compliant declaration of the payment-aggregator agreements and the absence of prohibited crypto-asset intermediation; audit trail of the inbound MT103 or ACH settlement into the Authorised Dealer account with matching transaction reference, ensuring no third-party interposition in economic ownership.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for non-resident shareholder capital injection: (a) the foreign subscriber instructs its bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer to the (Pty) Ltd's account held at a South African Authorised Dealer, with field 72/70 remittance data clearly stating 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION - INWARD FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT' and referencing the company name and registration number; (b) the BoP purpose code must be reported by the Authorised Dealer as 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital - Inflow'; (c) the bank is required to file the inward BoP3/BOP4 declaration with SARB/FinSurv within 30 days; (d) once the Authorised Dealer receives the remittance, the ZAR credit is booked at the prevailing market rate after confirmation of source-of-funds documentation; (e) for non-resident subscribers using loan contributions, a shareholder loan agreement denominated in foreign currency must be registered with the Authorised Dealer to obtain an Loan/External Liability reference, enabling later interest and capital repayment; (f) verification steps include matching the MT103 reference, obtaining a SWIFT confirmation from the issuing bank, and producing the share certificate or register entry to evidence the FDI status for future disinvestment and dividend remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational clearing rails: (a) standard outward vendor and content-acquisition payments use SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfers through the local Authorised Dealer after BoP declaration and supporting invoice; (b) for high-value repetitive international licensing of content libraries, a commercial documentary Letter of Credit may be issued via SWIFT MT700 to the non-resident seller, with presentation of transport-free service invoices, platform delivery evidence, and a certificate proving the licence grant; (c) local ZAR payments for domestic model fees, photographers, or AI cloud services settle via the real-time national payment system (RTCS) or Fast/EFT rails; (d) all outward current-account disbursements exceeding prescribed thresholds require SARS tax-clearance and an annual BoP form completed by the Authorised Dealer; (e) capital outflows such as acquisition of a foreign catalogue or IP buyout are treated as outward foreign direct investment and require FinSurv exchange-control approval before the MT103 release; (f) the entity should further standardise the use of ISO 20022 structured remittance advice to embed invoice, VAT/Tax Invoice number, and purpose codes, thereby preventing customs and SARB compliance queries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/ZAR forward contracts for current-account and balance-sheet exposures, executed with the local Authorised Dealer on the basis of approved underlying foreign-currency receivables or payables

USD/ZAR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by offshore counterparties solely through a FinSurv-approved external-account structure, noting that ZAR must remain non-deliverable offshore and such contracts are discouraged for a simple service-exporter treasury
Cross-currency swaps (USD/ZAR) and interest-rate swaps linked to a documented underlying commercial loan or foreign-currency asset, subject to Authorised Dealer confirmation and FinSurv reporting

Foreign-currency call accounts in USD/EUR/GBP with the South African Authorised Dealer used as a natural hedge for the stock-photo royalty receivable pool, thereby reducing spread and timing risk without bespoke derivative approval
Spot FX trade conversions executed on the interbank ZAR market for transaction-clearing of inbound and outbound royalty flows, with standing instruction to avoid speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Company (CIPC CoR 30.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues immediately after the statutory window; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers CIPC administrative strike-off and deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Filing (Part of Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the Annual Return (anniversary plus 30 business days)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with beneficial ownership filing obligations may result in administrative penalties, civil sanctions, and potential holding company liability for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory for public interest score (PIS) of 350 or more; PIS between 100 and 349 requires an independent review; PIS below 100 may be exempt from both audit and review unless otherwise triggered by shareholder action, holding company requirement, or contractual obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA) for public or widely held companies; IFRS for SMEs permitted for private companies with no public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A beneficial ownership register must be maintained on-site and updated whenever a beneficial owner changes or a transfer of shares alters indirect holding; the register is reconciled with the Annual Return filing to CIPC each year, and any undisclosed beneficial owner must be identified in the annual confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per year if audit trigger applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Section 11D R&D incentive grants a 150% deduction for qualifying research and development in software/AI. Small Business Corporation graduated rates: 0% on first ZAR 95,000; 7% up to ZAR 365,000; 21% up to ZAR 550,000; 27% above. Assessed losses carry forward indefinitely but can reduce no more than 80% of taxable income for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2022.
